I ported the C program to Zig in `src/main.zig`, and `build.sh` builds an optimized binary at `./app`. `node check.mjs` passes all 6 example cases. On a 52 MB input that mixed generated words with random bytes, the Zig output matched the original C build byte for byte. It ran in 0.11 s, versus 0.24 s for the C version.

One design difference from the C code: it reads all of standard input into memory first, rather than in 64 KB chunks. This makes peak memory roughly the input size plus the word
